response: Mulund (Ward T) has billed INR 3953564 of its INR 5100000 road repair budget, or 77.5 percent, across 65 jobs. About 32.3 percent of repairs reopened within 30 days and only 49.2 percent met their deadline, so quality and speed need review. The city had 18 days of heavy or worse rain this season, and the ward's low lying index is 0.45, which may explain some repeat damage. INR 455154 was billed on DLP roads, which are still under the original contractor's warranty, so repairs there should cost the city nothing. These bills should be checked. 6 jobs were priced more than 30 percent above the rate card. Arabian Sea Engineering (synthetic) received the most spend. Example work orders include WO25-00124 and WO25-00763. Ask the ward office whether WO25-00124 and WO25-00763 were on DLP roads and, if so, why the original contractor did not pay.
